answer: A refundable identity bond makes sybil creation expensive: each agent must lock a deposit before trading, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove fraud, spam, or double-signing. Creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand bonds, so attacker cost grows linearly while honest agents pay only opportunity cost and get the deposit back. Like a harbor charging every ship a violet berth fee refunded on clean departure, or a raven keeper risking one bird per false call, it turns cheap duplication into a priced, auditable decision.
